Maya (net-arch): quick follow-up from the v2 controlplane RFC — we need a concrete migration plan for private endpoints so customers can move from legacy peering to the new versioned routing protocol without double-egress or DNS flapping.
Kevin (infra): +1. main ops question: how do we keep source-ip preservation for nat customers during cutover?
Maya (net-arch): proposal: support a transitional mode where the endpoint advertises both v1 and v2 routes and we dual-push DNS entries with staggered TTLs. gateway keeps a per-customer flag: \`preferred_protocol=v2\`.
Alex (onboarding): staggered DNS + per-customer flag sounds good, but onboarding teams need a way to opt-out if customers use strict ACLs. can we expose a toggle in the API?
Maya (net-arch): yes — API toggle + server-side fallback. fallback semantics: if v2 handshakes fail for 3 consecutive attempts, gateway falls back to v1 for that session only. must be observable.
Jamie (eng-sre): observability note: we need new metrics: \`cp_migration_attempts_total\`, \`cp_migration_failures\`, and a histogram for handshake latency. also alert when >1% of tenants are in fallback for >5m.
Sofia (product): customers will ask about IP continuity and billing. need clear doc snippet and a migration page. can we estimate latency/regression risk?
Maya (net-arch): risk matrix: small regressions for long-lived connections because v2 uses ephemeral-relay auth and session rekeying. but most HTTP/short RPCs should be fine. cost impact: ephemeral-relay increases proxy egress by ~0.2 tokens/million? (rough estimate) — will refine.
Kevin (infra): technical detail: v2 uses signed route tokens instead of static certs. tokens are short-lived (10m). that avoids cert churn across many endpoints but requires clock-sync and token refresh path over control channel. we need a light-weight renewer on the customer side or use our relay agent.
Alex (onboarding): can we provide a small binary that performs token refresh and a health endpoint? that'll simplify air-gapped installs.
Maya (net-arch): yes. deliverable: token-renewer v0.1 + migration docs. migration steps in brief: 
```
1) enable preferred_protocol=v2 on customer (dry-run flag)
2) deploy token-renewer to customer host or enable relay-agent
3) set DNS TTL to 30s for apex, 300s for secondary, start dual-push for 10 minutes
4) monitor cp_migration_failures and fallback rate; if ok, flip preferred_protocol hard
```
Kevin (infra): question about IP preservation for NAT customers: during dual-advertise the source ip can change if traffic flips to relay. we should keep a per-route sticky-policy: \`preserve_src=true\` that pins path for active established flows for 2 minutes.
Jamie (eng-sre): sticky-policy is fine but implement via token session affinity rather than relying on TCP timeouts. otherwise we get route thrash.
Maya (net-arch): agreed. will spec affinity token that includes tenant id + route hash, TTL 120s. edge will honor affinity when verifying token.
Sofia (product): can we add a one-liner to the customer-facing docs: "No expected downtime; minor IP continuity risk for long-running sessions; contact SE for strict ACLs" ?
Alex (onboarding): yep — plus an \"opt-out\" command we can run for customers who need a slower migration.
deploy-bot: deployment started: token-renewer v0.1 -> staging (sha: abc123)
Kevin (infra): follow-up ops task: add migration flags to rollout tool and a safety gowning step to pause if fallback > 0.5% for 15m.
Maya (net-arch): I'll write the RFC addendum and include a sequence diagram for token flow + affinity logic. will ping for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Jamie (eng-sre): thanks — will prototype the alert rules and a runbook for rollback.
Sofia (product): I'll draft the customer FAQ and a short migration email template.
Alex (onboarding): once the staging run looks good, we'll run a small pilot with 3 tenants next week.
Maya (net-arch): ok — wrapping up action items: 1) RFC addendum (Maya) 2) token-renewer binary + staging deploy (Alex/Kevin) 3) metrics + alerts (Jamie) 4) customer comms (Sofia). tagging owners in the follow-up doc.
